channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: New York City Bans Horse-Drawn Carriages After Decade-Long Battle
item.description: New York’s City Council voted to ban horse-drawn carriages, ending a Central Park tourist staple dating to the 19th century after years of debate over the horses’ place on city streets. Bloomberg's Laura Nahmias explains. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Rio Tinto to Spend $1.9 Billion on Australian Bauxite Expansion
item.description: Rio Tinto Group will spend $1.9 billion to expand its bauxite mining operations in northern Australia, with the development of a new major mine to replace production from depleting projects.
item.dc:creator: Paul-Alain Hunt

item.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Oct. 23
item.description: Oil held its biggest gain in about a week as intensifying attacks on Saudi Arabia stoked fears of supply disruptions.
item.dc:creator: Kanoko Matsuyama

item.title: Asian Stocks to Slide on Tech Rout, Bonds Rally: Markets Wrap
item.description: Asian stocks were set to extend losses Friday, tracking a slump on Wall Street as a rout in technology giants and escalating Middle East hostilities drove investors toward the safety of bonds.
item.dc:creator: Toby Alder

item.title: Mickey Drexler on Decker Results and Retail Outlook
item.description: Mickey Drexler, Chair of Alex Mill and Former CEO and chair of J. Crew, tells Bloomberg that apparel retailers need to do more to give consumers a reason to buy. He says product, discounting and especially newness matter, while arguing that fashion has put too little emphasis on creativity and reinvention. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Affirm, Sam’s Club Strike Exclusive Buy Now, Pay Later Deal
item.description: Affirm is teaming up with Walmart’s Sam’s Club as the retailer’s exclusive buy-now, pay-later partner, just weeks before the key holiday shopping season kicks off. Affirm will serve as Sam’s Club’s exclusive BNPL provider in a multi-year agreement, starting in that role on Sam’s Club’s website in the coming weeks and rolling out to stores in 2027, according to a statement Thursday that didn’t disclose terms of the deal. Max Levchin, Founder & CEO of Affirm, joins Bloomberg Businessweek Daily to discuss. He speaks with Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Australian Growth Likely Slower Than Expected, Chalmers Says
item.description: Australia’s growth will likely be slower than the 1.75% forecast in May’s budget, Australian Treasurer Jim Chalmers said Friday, as a series of rate hikes and rising inflation start to bite on the economy.
item.dc:creator: Nasteho Said

item.title: Kroger CFO: We Are an Agent for the Consumer
item.description: Kroger CFO David Kennerley discusses the company plans to invest $5 billion in consumer value, including affordable groceries and simpler promotions, while seeking to fund the effort through $4 billion in structural cost savings. Kennerley said the company is seeing a slight uptick in inflation but remains within the range it projected earlier in the year, and will accept supplier price increases only when justified. He speaks with Romaine Bostick in "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Huntington Bancshares CEO Stephen Steinour on 3Q Results
item.description: Huntington Bank shares were little changed after the company reported revenue below expectations and earnings per share in line. CEO Steve Steinour said the results reinforce confidence in meeting financial targets and delivering sustained earnings growth. He cited growth and the integration of the Cadence and Veritex partnerships, while explaining that stronger competition has made some lending unattractive. He speaks with Romaine Bostick & Jess Menton on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: A Tesla-SpaceX Merger Doesn’t Add Up
item.description: Elon Musk is eager to consolidate Tesla and SpaceX, but recent earnings numbers show how odd that merger would be, Bloomberg Opinion columnist Liam Denning says. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: TD Cowen Analyst on Chipotle Downgrade
item.description: Andrew Charles discusses TD Cowen’s downgrade of Chipotle to Hold, citing concerns about sales trends. He said the company’s recent same-store sales have benefited from creative campaigns, including four annual limited-time protein offerings, value initiatives and a new chief marketing officer, but he expected these efforts to deliver stronger results in the fourth quarter and argued that growth will become harder in 2027 as Chipotle laps those drivers and must rely on less-proven initiatives. He speaks with Romaine Bostick & Jess Menton on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Jane Street, HRT Are Spending Billions to Win in AI Era
item.description: High-frequency trading firms are even building their own data centers as they compete for an edge in the AI era.
item.dc:creator: Katherine Doherty, Dina Bass and Justina Lee

item.title: Shopify-Like IPO Successes Becoming Rare in Canada, Nowlan Says
item.description: Canada will struggle to find another stock-market success story like Shopify Inc. as the country grapples with a public-listing drought and a delisting trend, according to Daniel Nowlan at National Bank Capital Markets.
item.dc:creator: Stephanie Hughes

item.title: Moderna, Merck Fall After Melanoma Data Leak
item.description: Moderna and Merck shares plummeted after data on the companies' personalized melanoma vaccine wasn't enough to prove to investors that a new era of cancer treatments has arrived. Michelle Fay Cortez has more on "Bloomberg The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Powerful Tibet Earthquake Kills 18 People and Injures 32 Others
item.description: At least 18 people were killed after a magnitude-7.0 earthquake struck the Tibetan Plateau in China on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Brian K. Sullivan and Jacob Gu

item.title: Typhoon Champi Shuts Taiwan’s $5 Trillion Stock Market
item.description: Taiwan’s stock exchange will shut Friday as Typhoon Champi approaches the island, bringing heavy rainfall and strong winds that prompted authorities to shut offices and schools in the capital city of Taipei.
item.dc:creator: Miaojung Lin and Mary Hui

item.title: Yen Jumps as Traders Seek Safety Amid Global Flight From Risk
item.description: The yen surged, outperforming all its major counterparts on Thursday, as a selloff in global equities boosted demand for havens.
item.dc:creator: Ran Li and Anya Andrianova

item.title: Nasdaq 100 Drops 3% as Risk-Off Dominates With Oil Prices Rising
item.description: US stocks fell on Thursday as escalating concern about the Mideast conflict pushed oil futures higher, spurring inflation fears with US midterm elections less than two weeks away. Meta Platforms Inc. tumbled as investors parsed its results along with the rest of the latest batch of technology earnings for evidence that massive spending on AI is paying off.
item.dc:creator: Felice Maranz

item.title: Stocks Fall as AI Jitters Ease Bets on Fed Hikes: Markets Wrap
item.description: Wall Street shunned stocks as a technology rout and Middle East risks drove investors to the safety of bonds, reducing bets on another Federal Reserve rate hike in 2026.
item.dc:creator: Rita Nazareth

item.title: BlackRock's Senra on Investment Shifts, Wealth Transfer
item.description: Armando Senra, Head of the Americas Institutional Business at BlackRock, said family offices generally view geopolitical tensions as a source of short-term market and allocation effects, rather than a reason for major long-term portfolio changes. He said investors are attentive to current events but are maintaining broader trends seen among institutional clients: expanding private-market exposure with greater diversification and using ETFs for both active and index strategies. He speaks with Romaine Bostick & Jess Menton on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)
